title: intermittent-quota-siphon-from-stale-meter-window-during-fast-route-fanout
creator: Aisha Kumar
summary: Customers observed short-lived unexplained quota exhaustion for org-scoped keys when many route variants are invoked concurrently. Initial metrics show per-org allowance being consumed without corresponding meter increments; appears correlated with rapid route fanout and route TTL refreshes on the policy cache.
severity_notes: Affects billing and customer-visible throttling; multiple customers reported transient 429s during high-concurrency requests causing production degradation. Occurs non-deterministically under high route churn and autoscaling events.
reproducer_steps: 1) Create org with standard per-org token allowance (e.g., 1M tokens/day).
2) Configure application to fan out requests to 8 route variants that share same org key but different route tags.
3) Run parallel clients to emit short bursts of 200 requests across routes with randomized route selection and route rename/alias operations in the same timeframe.
4) Observe org allowance drop and 429 responses without equivalent increments in the usage ingestion dashboard.
observed_logs: 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z [enforcer-34] WARN allowance-check fail: org=org_42 key=cred_123 route=route-A computed_allowance=-200
2026-02-18T15:12:03Z [meter-agg] INFO ingest-skip: shard=7 reason=cache-stale route=route-A possibly-duplicated
Sample backend metric: per-org-meter-commit-rate shows drops during bursts while enforcer-count shows immediate allowance decrements.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-21: Initial triage by SRE and billing team. Replayed synthetic load in staging; reproduced under high-concurrency + route aliasing.

Hypothesis A: race between policy cache TTL refresh and in-flight enforcement path causing double-subtractive accounting where transient in-memory allowance could be decremented locally and also reconciled by the shard aggregator as a separate debit on replay.

Hypothesis B: overlap of per-route temporary keys created for aliases leads to separate meter-key namespaces that the enforcer treats as distinct, but the aggregator consolidates them later in a way that produces misattributed negative allowance.
Added detailed log tracing to enforcer, meter-agg, and route-cache to capture request-id, lease-id, and policy-version for each decision.
root_cause: Under race conditions during rapid route alias/rename operations, the enforcer's fastpath applies a local allowance decrement based on a stale route->policy mapping while the policy cache refresh path issues reconciliatory decrements leading to double-counting. Additionally, newly minted alias keys used during the refresh are temporarily billed under separate meter keys which the aggregator later folds, resulting in apparent siphoning from the org allowance without matching meter ingest events in short windows.
work_items: 1) Mark: Add an atomic enforcement token (lease id) per request that is persisted to the shard metadata prior to applying local allowance decrement (safety net for replay).
2) Marcus: Ensure route-cache refresh is serialized per-key to avoid concurrent cache split where legacy and new alias keys are both active for the same logical route during the same request window.
3) Billing team: Emit explicit 'tentative-debit' and 'finalize-debit' events so the aggregator can idempotently dedupe reconciliations.
4) Add integration test that simulates concurrent alias/rename and high-fanout calls validating no net negative allowance and that meter ingest equals enforcer debits in the aggregator.
proposed_fixes: - Short term hotfix: backfill reconciliation job to detect negative org allowance anomalies and create compensating events (audit-only, avoid auto-credit without manual review).

- Medium term: implement per-request enforcement lease persisted to shard storage with TTL; enforcer must check lease uniqueness before applying a local decrement and include lease id in meter events.

- Long term: refactor policy cache update path to perform coordinated swap (prepare->swap->drain) so in-flight requests see consistent policy versions and alias key transitions are atomic at the routing layer.
mitigation_and_rollout: 1) Deploy logging and lease-check instrumentation to canary region (us-west-2) behind feature flag. 2) Run targeted traffic for affected customers and monitor per-org allowance vs ingest parity dashboards. 3) If stable for 48h, roll out lease atomic enforcement globally and enable aggregator dedupe based on lease ids.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease uniqueness; integration test in staging with 10k synthetic concurrent requests + alias churn; end-to-end validation comparing enforcer-debits vs aggregator-ingest for every request-id during test windows.
metrics_to_watch: meter-aggregator-dedup-counts (should increase once dedupe enabled then drop)
policy-cache-refresh-latency and concurrent-refreshes-per-key (should go to 0 for key after serialization)
notes: We intentionally avoid auto-crediting during hotfix to prevent potential abuse. Any corrective financial adjustments will be handled by billing ops after manual review. Communications: drafted customer-only postmortem to be reviewed by legal and support once fixes are validated.
